idiom_name: protocol DAO + enum-keyed factory function returning any UserDAO (NSPersistentContainer for the store stack)
implementation_notes: A protocol plus an enum store key and a factory function returning any UserDAO is the whole pattern: Swift's protocols and value types remove any need for an abstract factory class, and dependencies are normally injected through initializers. On Apple platforms the store half is the framework's: NSPersistentContainer encapsulates the managed object model, persistent store coordinator and contexts, and loadPersistentStores selects the concrete store descriptions, so a DAO family over NSManagedObjectContext (or over SQLite/HTTP clients) is handed the context by the container instead of building its own. Keep the factory function at the composition root - app initialization or scene setup - and return the protocol existential.
pitfalls: any UserDAO existentials box the DAO; in hot paths or with associated types, a generic parameter (some UserDAO or <D: UserDAO>) avoids the allocation and keeps static dispatch.
NSManagedObjectContext is not Sendable and is queue-confined; passing one into an actor or background task requires container.performBackgroundTask, or the DAO family must be main-actor bound.
Protocol plus factory hides the store but not the error model: throwing DAOs must translate NSError/SQLite/HTTP failures into one error type or callers keep store knowledge.
